head: b5c2b62d828e19ec7183ba7fc08ab5dd6c4ee806
summary:
SL-042 at b5c2b62 does what it owes, and I checked it against real drives as well as its tests. I rebuilt it from scratch in Release (0 warnings). The full Core.Tests suite passes 188/188 with 0 skipped. The timing test's 10 reads of 100,000 children took 9.16–9.80 ms against the 250 ms limit. The 5M-entry budget test held 652.1 MiB retained, with a 678.4 MiB peak, against 800 MiB. Fitness: all 31 rules hold.

For independent real contact I wrote a throwaway console probe in %TEMP%. It ran the slice's exact Core DLL (hash-matched) over C:\Windows (346,280 entries) and C:\Program Files (87,862 entries). It checked every folder against oracles built outside the store:
- **Dedup:** file IDs read through a handle agreed with the listing IDs on 188,123 files. The store's first-seen duplicate flag agreed with the probe's own first-seen decision on 188,532/188,532 and 77,391/77,391 files.
- **Folder totals:** the probe summed the store's leaves itself, using its own dedup and its own charge rule. That gave 0 mismatches in size, on-disk size or file count across 157,748 + 10,441 folders, and the root equalled Totals.
- **Membership:** listing each readable folder through System.IO gave exactly its child block, with 0 differences in 157,696 + 10,439 folders.
- **Ordered reads:** ChildrenLargestFirst was correct on every folder (order, the listing-order tiebreak, on-disk values, shares, 0 share for a 0-byte parent, shares summing to 1). The slowest read, WinSxS\Manifests with 38,958 children, took 13.1 ms.
- **Repeatability:** three back-to-back scans of C:\Windows gave identical totals in all 157,748 folders (0 moved). So the single-writer order the no-go spike warned about does hold.
- **Published exe:** it ran through the real entry point (read-window.ps1 on C:\Program Files) with EXIT 0 and Completed, and its top-level rows add up to the totals.

Sizes read through a handle differed from the store in 2 C:\Windows folders (on-disk off by 15,048 B and 3,632 B, file-level listing values) and in 4 Program Files folders (a live OneDrive log that grew). Both are outside this slice's criteria.

One case is only half built: the real-NTFS half of case 8. The critique allowed dropping it, because local NTFS lists every folder at 0 bytes, so that test could not fail.

A loop worth naming: the index shows 29 design-slice attempts with no caused_by and no changes. Build-slice says 27 of them hit the provider's session limit.

checks.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 build FsAnalyser.slnx -c Release --no-incremental
checks.evidence: Build succeeded, 0 warnings, 0 errors. The Core and Tests DLLs were stamped 05:54:25 on 2026-09-26, the time of the run.

checks.what: Full default Core.Tests suite in Release
checks.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests -c Release --no-build --logger "trx;LogFileName=full.trx" --results-directory %TEMP%\sl042-validate
checks.evidence: Passed! Failed 0, Passed 188, Skipped 0, Total 188, 9 s. The trx shows every ScanStoreRollupTests case passing, along with HardlinkTests (2,0), (2,1) and (3,2), LinkTests, UnreadableFolderTests, the timing test and the budget test.

checks.what: Criterion 6 timing test output, read from the trx StdOut
checks.command: same run; trx UnitTestResult Output/StdOut for ScanStoreRollupTimingTests
checks.evidence: 'Release build, high-resolution clock True. 10 reads of 100,000 children, the first cold, in ms: 9.39, 9.80, 9.31, 9.31, 9.58, 9.66, 9.76, 9.58, 9.58, 9.16; slowest 9.80, budget 250'

checks.what: Memory budget test with the three rollup columns at 5M entries
checks.evidence: 'entries 5,000,000, files 4,510,000, duplicate names 200,000 ... folder totals on every row, one folder of 100,000 read largest first; retained 652.1 MiB, sampled peak 678.4 MiB, budget 800 MiB'
31 rules checked against 65 files: every declared rule holds, including the three settled by SL-042. Two matches fell in comments and were not counted.

checks.what: Independent real-tree oracle over C:\Windows: handle-route IDs vs listing IDs, and the dedup decision
checks.command: throwaway net10 console in %TEMP%\sl042-validate\probe referencing src/FsAnalyser.Core/bin/Release/net10.0-windows/FsAnalyser.Core.dll (SHA-256 4B7C3A40..., identical to the build), run as probe.exe C:\Windows
checks.evidence: Scan Completed: 346,280 entries, Files 188,532, Folders 157,747, 52 unreadable. Handle opens (FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES, FileIdInfo and FileStandardInfo): 188,123 OK, 409 failed with error 5. Listing FileId equalled the handle FileId in 188,123/188,123. The store's HardlinkDuplicate flag agreed with the probe's handle-ID first-seen decision on 188,532/188,532 files (133,540 first names, 54,992 later names).

checks.what: Every folder's rollups on real C:\Windows vs an independent brute-force sum (probe's own dedup and charge rule over the store's leaf sizes)
checks.evidence: 157,748 folders, 0 mismatches in RolledSize, RolledOnDisk or FilesBelow. Root rollups equal Totals (42,362,707,214 / 40,979,605,016 / 188,532).

checks.what: Folder rollups vs handle-route sizes, a check of leaf fidelity and not of this slice's criteria
checks.command: probe.exe C:\Windows and probe.exe "C:\Program Files" (oracle B)
checks.evidence: C:\Windows: 157,721 of 157,723 untainted folders match exactly. WinSxS\Manifests is off by -15,048 B on disk and one powershell.common folder by -3,632 B on disk; logical sizes are exact. Program Files: 10,437/10,441 match; the 4 that differ are the chain above a live OneDrive FileSyncHelper\logs file that grew 3,738 B between the scan and the probe. Oracle A matched on the same folders, so the rollup is exact and the difference is in file-level listing values the Scanner does not probe (below 64 MiB, non-zero allocation). That is pre-existing SizeProbe policy, outside C1-C6.

checks.what: Membership: each readable folder's System.IO listing vs the store's child block (names)
checks.evidence: C:\Windows: 157,696 folders, 0 differ, 0 IO errors. Program Files: 10,439 folders, 0 differ.

checks.what: ChildrenLargestFirst on every real folder: length, unique children, OnDisk equal to RolledOnDisk, share equal to OnDisk/parent (0 when parent 0, never NaN), order with Entry tiebreak, children summing to the parent, shares summing to 1
checks.evidence: C:\Windows: 157,748 folders, 0 bad, slowest single read 13.13 ms. The widest folder, WinSxS\Manifests (38,958 children), read in 9.77–13.18 ms over 10 reads. Program Files: 10,441 folders, 0 bad. Root shares at the top: System32 29.08%, WinSxS 24.32%.

checks.what: Independent oracle over C:\Program Files (30 links, 224 later hardlink names)
checks.evidence: Completed: 87,862 entries, Links 30, 2 unreadable. IDs agree 77,391/77,391; dedup agrees 77,391/77,391; oracle A shows 0 mismatches in 10,441 folders; root rollups equal Totals.

checks.evidence: All three runs gave the identical Totals (188,532 files; 42,362,713,756 B; 40,979,627,792 B on disk). Across 157,748 common folders: on-disk moved 0, more than 1 MiB 0, more than 10 MiB 0, file count moved 0. The spike measured 68 folders moving more than 10 MiB with 16 workers.

EXIT 0, status Completed, files 77,391, folders 10,440, links 30, bytes 34,100,818,396, on disk 34,154,406,672. 53 top-level rows, 1 unreadable, and the rows sum to the totals (final true). The window reads 'Finished', '31.8 GB in files, taking 31.8 GB on disk'. CountersText shows an older progress sample: the known pre-existing issue.

checks.what: Real-NTFS half of case 8: a folder that owns a directory allocation is in no total
checks.evidence: Not built at build-slice (m7 disposition). Build-slice's probe with the project's DirectoryReader found local NTFS lists every folder at 0/0, so such a test could not fail here. I did not re-measure folder stated sizes.

Exit 1: slice/SL-040 is still unmerged, so the semantic merge point (Append clears HardlinkDuplicate, AddFlags refuses it) was not exercised. It is documented in docs/design/SL-042-folder-totals.md, 'Merging with slice/SL-040'.
Only the engine's own .taad/slices/SL-042 files show. No tracked file was changed; the temp probes and publish output were removed.

criteria.criterion: 1. Roll up folder totals (C1): a chain 10,000 folders deep with one file at every level
criteria.how: AChainTenThousandFoldersDeepRollsEveryFileUpToEveryAncestor passed in Release (0.42 s). It checks the Expected oracle, CheckStructure, and hand-computed triangle totals at every depth.

criteria.criterion: 2. C1: one folder with 100,000 direct children, 1,000 of them subfolders holding files
criteria.how: AFolderWithAHundredThousandChildrenRollsUpAcrossPageBoundaries passed: more than 3 pages, FilesBelow and per-subfolder totals asserted.

criteria.criterion: 3. C1: empty folders, nested empty folders, an empty root, and a seeded ~50k mixed tree, with the oracle run after every append on a small one
criteria.how: All 4 rows of EmptyAndMixedTreesMatchTheOracleAtEveryCut passed. The 400-entry tree is checked after every append; the 50,000-entry tree asserts every shape is present.

criteria.criterion: 4. C2, C3: one ID under three names in three folders, fixed order
criteria.how: OneIdUnderThreeNamesInThreeFoldersIsChargedOnceToTheFirstNamesFolder passed: first holder x for all three, only a is charged, Files counted at x, a, y, b, z, c, top and root. On real data, the store's dedup agreed with a handle-ID first-seen oracle on 188,532 + 77,391 files.

criteria.criterion: 5. C2, C3: names sharing an ancestor or a parent
6. C2: IDs that must not match (0, all-ones, widened 64-bit all-ones, same low half)
criteria.how: IdsThatMustNotMatchAreEachCharged passed. I read HasFileId (ScanStore.cs:147) and it rejects all three sentinels.

criteria.criterion: 7. C4: a link (5000/8192) and an Unreadable folder (4096/4096) beside a normal file, plus appends under a File, Link or Unreadable parent
criteria.how: ALinkAndAnUnreadableFolderAreLeavesThatAddNothing passed; the three appends throw InvalidOperationException. The real-tree LinkTests and UnreadableFolderTests rollup assertions also passed.

criteria.criterion: 8a. C1, C4: a readable folder stating its own non-zero size (synthetic 4096/4096) adds nothing of it
criteria.how: AFolderThatStatesItsOwnSizeAddsNothingOfIt passed. Charges() (ScanStore.cs:273) is true only for a non-duplicate File. My real oracle A charges folders 0 and matched every real folder.

criteria.criterion: 8b. C1, C4: a real NTFS folder large enough to own a directory allocation adds nothing of it
criteria.how: Not built (m7 disposition). Build-slice measured that local NTFS lists folders at 0/0, so the precondition cannot be produced on this machine. I did not check it.

criteria.criterion: 9. C5: mixed files and subfolders with equal on-disk sizes and one hardlink duplicate, read three times
criteria.how: ChildrenAreReadLargestFirstWithEqualSizesInListingOrder passed (67 children, 60 ties). On real data the order and tiebreak held in all 168,189 folders.

criteria.criterion: 10. C5: shares of 3/4 and 1/4 (exact), 1/3 (within 1e-12), summing to 1
criteria.how: EachChildsShareIsItsOnDiskBytesOverTheFolders passed. On real data every share equalled OnDisk/parent exactly, and the shares of each non-zero folder summed to 1 within 1e-9.

criteria.criterion: 11. C5: a parent whose on-disk total is 0 (empty, only duplicates, online-only files), plus a File, Link or Unreadable passed as the folder
criteria.how: AFolderWithNothingOnDiskGivesEveryChildAZeroShare passed. On real data no share was NaN, and every child of a 0 total had share 0.0.

criteria.criterion: 12. C6: 100,000 children with many ties, 10 reads with the cold one counted, Release build
criteria.how: The Release run reported 9.16–9.80 ms against 250 ms, and the output line records 'Release build'.

criteria.criterion: 13. C1-C4 through the real Scanner on NTFS temp trees with per-folder rollup assertions, root == Totals, TopLevelRow == rollup
criteria.how: Scans.AssertChargedBytesAreTheTotals runs in every real-tree test, and all 188 passed. I also ran my own independent real scans of C:\Windows and C:\Program Files: 0 rollup mismatches, root == Totals.

criteria.criterion: 14. C1: 5,000,000 entries carrying the three rollup columns, with one 100,000-child folder
criteria.how: The budget test passed: retained 652.1 MiB, sampled peak 678.4 MiB, against 800 MiB. It measures the GC heap, not process private bytes.

planned.evidence: The synthetic tests (10,000-deep chain, 100,000-wide folder, empty and nested empty folders, 50k mixed tree) passed against a brute-force oracle built from the input stream. On real data, a brute-force sum computed outside the store matched RolledSize, RolledOnDisk and FilesBelow in all 157,748 C:\Windows and 10,441 Program Files folders (0 mismatches).

OneIdUnderThreeNamesInThreeFolders...: root equals one copy, and only the first name's folder is charged. On real data the store's duplicate flag matched a handle-ID first-seen oracle on 188,532/188,532 and 77,391/77,391 files. Three back-to-back C:\Windows scans moved 0 folders, so first-seen is repeatable under the single-writer Scanner.

The same test asserts Files at every level (x, a, y, b, z, c, top, root), including the 0-byte names. HardlinkTests asserts per-folder files on real NTFS. The real FilesBelow matched the oracle at every folder (54,992 later names in C:\Windows).

ALinkAndAnUnreadableFolderAreLeavesThatAddNothing: 5000/8192 link and 4096/4096 unreadable folder; the parent equals the file alone, neither has children, and appends under them throw. The real LinkTests and UnreadableFolderTests pass with rollup assertions. Deviation, as declared: a folder listed in part before its error keeps what was listed. It was opened, so it is not the 'could not be opened' case.

Ordering (67 children, ties in listing order), exact 3/4, 1/4 and 1/3 shares, and 0-byte parents (empty, only duplicates, online-only) all pass. On real data every one of 168,189 folders read correctly, with no NaN.
Timed test in a Release build: 10 reads of 100,000 children took 9.16–9.80 ms (budget 250 ms). The real widest folder (38,958 children) read in at most 13.18 ms.

obligations.evidence: The 10,000-deep chain test passed in my Release run.
The 100,000-children test passed in my Release run.
The three-names test passed. Real dedup agreed with the handle-ID oracle on every file.
The link and unreadable-leaf test passed.
The synthetic half passed. The real-NTFS half was not built (m7) and is listed in not_reached.
The ordering test passed. The real order and tiebreak were correct in all folders.
The share test passed. Real shares were exact and summed to 1.
The zero-share test passed. There were no NaN shares on real data.
Release: 9.16–9.80 ms over 10 reads. The test sits in the non-parallel MemoryBudget collection ([Collection(nameof(MemoryBudget))]).
AssertChargedBytesAreTheTotals runs CheckStructure, root == Totals, and TopLevelRow == rollup on every real-tree scan; all passed. My independent real scans agree.
Retained 652.1 MiB, peak 678.4 MiB, against 800 MiB in my run.

Append returns firstHolder and Posted, and CorrectSizes posts up the corrected row's chain (ScanStore.cs:257-265). HardlinkTests (2,1) and (3,2), the stale-first-name cases, passed. The real scans probed first holders and matched the oracles.
HasFileId rejects 0, all-ones and (0, ulong.MaxValue) (ScanStore.cs:147-150). The Scanner's _settled set uses it at all three sites (Scanner.cs diff).
FilesBelow(file) = 1 and link = 0 (ScanStore.Rollup.cs:39-48). The children-sum invariant held in CheckStructure and in the real oracle.
Totals flow only through Credit(entry, posted, inPlace) (Scanner.cs). Root rollups equalled Totals on both real scans and in the published exe's top-level sums.
CheckParent (ScanStore.cs:278-295) runs before any write. AParentMustAlreadyBeInTheStoreAndOnlyTheRootHasNone passed.

not_reached: The real-NTFS half of case 8 (a folder that owns a directory allocation) was not checked. Build-slice measured that local NTFS lists every folder at 0/0. A volume that reports folder sizes (for example the opt-in SMB-LOOPBACK rig) was not run.
Process private-bytes peak at 5M entries was not measured against the spike's 1 GiB. The budget test measures GC-heap retained and peak (652.1 / 678.4 MiB) against 800 MiB.
No full-drive scan (C:\, about 2.4M files) was run. My real scans were C:\Windows (346,280 entries) and C:\Program Files (87,862), both well under 5M and without any folder of 100,000 real children.

In C:\Windows, 409 files denied a handle open (error 5). Their sizes and IDs could not be checked by the handle oracle, which leaves 25 folders tainted for the handle-size comparison. The rollup-arithmetic oracle still covered them, using the listing IDs.
Non-NTFS or ID-less volumes (FAT, SMB with 0 IDs) were not scanned; only the synthetic tests cover ID 0.
The semantic merge with the unmerged slice/SL-040 (Append clears HardlinkDuplicate, AddFlags refuses it) was not exercised.
Nothing in the window reads ChildrenLargestFirst yet, so the screen's half of the 0.5 s tree budget is unmeasured.
Reading the rollups from another thread while a scan runs is outside the stated contract and was not tested.

Under 64 MiB the Scanner keeps listing values rather than probing. On-disk differences from the handle route were seen in 2 C:\Windows folders (WinSxS\Manifests off by 15,048 B, a powershell.common folder off by 3,632 B). They are file-level, pre-existing and outside C1-C6, and I did not identify which files cause them.
